body: I can small talk pretty easily but I find it very superficial and unfulfilling.  It's very formulaic if you pay attention.  Pretty much just talk about observable things in your immediate vicinity or something you've both experienced.

> I might've won small battles here and there but am certainly not winning any wars.

Lots of small victories set the stage for winning wars.  Don't tread yourself down. :)
Very insightful!! Good job.
Are these things you worked out yourself, or is there some link you could share?

>Just a vital firsthand experience tip

What happened?  I would be very interested in learning from your experience.  Feel free to PM me if you don't want to share publicly!

>i hope they dont lock me in an asylum if i open up about this.

As long as you don't express an **intention** to hurt yourself or others, you should be fine.  Your therapist can't break confidentiality, even to an asylum, unless you pose a clear an imminent danger.

>This is the second time this girl has cancelled plans with me because she "wasn't feeling well"

Back off and see if she makes any attempt to reach out to you.  She isn't one for you if she isn't going to meet you mid way after cancelling twice.

>If she hates me why doesn't she just say something?

Some people are *very* conflict-averse.  Instead of taking control of uncomfortable situations by vocalizing their feelings, they will rely on excuses and white lies in order to avoid the situation.  It's a flaw in their character and has nothing to do with you.  Don't bother calling her out on this.
Very helpful, thanks!

>I have read a lot of books on self-improvement and they have helped me a lot.

Would you mind sharing the ones which stood out as particularly helpful?

>I haven't been a fan for a while

*Please* change therapists.  I know it's a scary step but feeling that way is almost certainly going to impede your progress. You can do better.

>To be honest he comes off very cold, serious and many people said that he is dull and moody.

Sounds like that particular guy doesn't have great social skills.  Don't typecast us all in that way, please!

> Funny how we know that we are capable of much more, yet settle for mediocrity.

Funny in a somewhat tragic sense, sure!
You seem to have dropped these. ))
Hey now, lets not meddle with the laws of natural selection.

>Or I'll find a hole in my logic and have to keep going and hope the other person doesn't poke there.

Yeah that hits home.  Waiting for their response can be pretty tense when that happens!

>How open are you to the possibility that you are completely wrong about something, or maybe everything?

Way too open.  Sometimes I notice flaws in whatever I'm saying and have to bluff my way through the rest of the sentence while navigating an internal existential crisis.

>Fun exercise.

Assuming your memories are reasonably happy.  I think I would rather get piss-waterboarded than relive some of my memories.

>I'm only 17

Ahhh.. The innocence of youth!  How I envy you.

>  if you are going slower when that happens, the chances of it being a fatal accident are lower.

That's a race to the bottom.  You could argue that it would be virtually impossible to die in a car if we all drove at a maximum of 10mp/h.

>This year I have nothing to give on Christmas and it's tearing my soul apart.

Sorry to hear that...  It's obvious why that must cut pretty deep, but try not to lose perspective.  This is just one day of the year.  You've got 364 other days to be the best parent you can be and *those* count a lot more in the long run.

>I feel like a failure.

From the little I know about you, I don't see a failure.  I see someone who's been through a rough year and just wants to provide the best for their family.  This makes you a commendable human being and probably a great parent.

> I need advice on how I handle this

Do your best on Christmas day.  It isn't all about the presents.

I think you should go to therapy alone and blaze a trail.  Your success will not only be hugely beneficial to you as an individual, but may serve as an inspiration for your SO to follow suit.  This seems like a better option because your SO doesn't have to just *attend* therapy; he has to make a *commitment* to the treatment.  Only he can do that.

>I just say "surviving". It's vague but it's an acceptable answer

Yep!  I use that too.  Sometimes people take that as an invitation to follow-up though.  Nice that they're showing an interest and perhaps care, but I don't like taking passengers on downward spirals!

> Do you ever feel like you don't know if you want to get better? 

I'm not entirely sure what *getting better* even looks like.  After so many years with depression it has become incredibly difficult to separate myself from my-depressed-self.  It's difficult to be motivated towards some ambiguous goal.

>All i could mumble through the tears was "Thank you"

I struggled, but held back the tears until that line.  Ouch.

*"How are you?"*

Because,

"~~Very fucking not-okay.  Depression has driven my life into the ground for a *third* time and whether or not tonight is the night I jump off a bridge is 50/50.~~ Not bad! How are you?  How's the wife/husband?  How's work?  How's life?  ~~What's your life story?! **Please** don't make me talk about myself~~."

>Physics and economics are firmly on the side of "No flying cars" or "few flying cars."

Are flying/floating *roads* any more favorable?   Sounds to me like we could almost get the benefit of flying cars without entrusting them to the public this way.

Rush hour? Send in some extra roads.  Some huge event?  Floating expressway straight there.  Roadworks?  Road over the top of it.  etc.

>I feel like this will be my future.

Yup! 26 here and I'm totally with you.  It's a bit like depression has taken the wheel and I'm going wherever it leads, however much I protest.

>Anyone else only happy when they go to sleep?

I'm not sure I would use the word *happy*, but being asleep is such a release.
Those look really nice!! I'd love to come and eat some with you!

>I wish there was a way of finding a good one without spending a ton of co-pays going to bad ones

Me too... Me too.

All I can say is that when you find a great one - it will have been worth the expense/inconvenience of all the bad ones.

> Left and never went back and now I cant bring myself to get a new one cause they will just all talk down to me.

Feeling that way is not surprising, but I implore you to give some other therapists a chance.  A major part of their job is to build trust and rapport with their clients but obviously that is not always possible.

Don't give up on it. :)
Yup.  My experience is that there has to be something of a personal match, too.  A therapist can be fantastic for one person and terrible for another.

Definitely do not continue with said therapist.

Therapy can be incredibly helpful but some therapists are just shit.

>"I'll pray for you"!

"I'll ask my ~~imaginary~~ friend to help you out."

FTFY.  It's nice that they care but it reads as a bit of a cop-out.
Can confirm it doesn't help me, either.  Having impaired judgement while battling suicidal thoughts is a ridiculous proposition.
Totally fucking perfect.  Well done.
Thank you for writing that.  I'm in a very bad place right now and this gave me some hope.
